recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Approvals service module
recommended_phases.rationale: Add web/src/modules/approvals/ with IApprovalsService + ApprovalsService (listPending filters SUBMITTED non-owner rows; approve/reject delegate to ILeaveService) and index.ts. Depends only on existing leave/employee/shared-types. No UI yet.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Approvals service unit tests
recommended_phases.rationale: Vitest coverage beside the service: pending filter (excludes own + non-SUBMITTED), approve/reject delegation, and rejected-decision failure path.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — RequireApprover route guard
recommended_phases.rationale: Add presentation/guards/RequireApprover.tsx (MANAGER|ADMIN only, else redirect) + test. Depends on auth context and shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — ApprovalsPage + route wiring
recommended_phases.rationale: Add ApprovalsPage (list, approve/reject buttons, empty state, drill-in link) and register /approvals route in App.tsx wrapped in RequireAuth + RequireApprover.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — ApprovalsPage tests + dashboard link
recommended_phases.rationale: Vitest coverage for the page (empty queue, approve/reject update, EMPLOYEE route rejection) and add the role-gated dashboard link.

app_notes: Application slice for the manager approvals queue (web/ only). New module web/src/modules/approvals/ owns IApprovalsService/ApprovalsService: listPending(profile) filters the existing role-scoped GET /leaves result to SUBMITTED requests not raised by the caller, and approve(id)/reject(id) delegate verbatim to the existing ILeaveService (reusing api-client approveLeave/rejectLeave — no new endpoints). Presentation adds RequireApprover guard (MANAGER|ADMIN, route-level, not link-only), ApprovalsPage (list + approve/reject + drill-in link + explicit empty state), and a role-gated dashboard link. Dependencies flow inward: presentation -> modules -> infrastructure; approvals depends on leave/employee/shared-types only. No circular edges. getAvailableLeaveActions is reused (not duplicated) for the approve/reject action matrix; role comes from EmployeeProfile (GET /employees/me), never JWT decoding.

open_questions.question: Should the approvals queue filter to SUBMITTED-only in the service, or rely on the backend's role-scoped GET /leaves and filter client-side?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether ApprovalsService.listPending must re-filter by status/ownership or can trust the API response; affects the empty-state and "row leaves queue after decision" behavior.
candidate_options: Filter SUBMITTED + non-owner in ApprovalsService (defensive, matches 'awaiting decision' semantics)
Trust GET /leaves role scoping and only exclude own requests
Add a status query param to the existing getLeaves call

open_questions.question: After approve/reject, should the row be removed from the queue or re-rendered with the new status?
open_questions.impact: Affects ApprovalsPage state update logic and the "row reflects new status or leaves the queue" acceptance criterion.
candidate_options: Remove the decided row from local state (leaves the queue)
Replace the row with the returned updated view (reflects new status)
Re-fetch the full list after each decision

auth_contract: Role-gated route access only (no new API endpoints). Identity/role come from the already-fetched EmployeeProfile (GET /employees/me) held in the auth session — never decoded from the JWT in the browser. EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. The /approvals route is wrapped in RequireAuth (session presence) plus a new RequireApprover guard that redirects any role other than MANAGER or ADMIN, so an EMPLOYEE visiting the route directly sees no other employee's data.
error_response_contract: No new API endpoints; the page surfaces existing ApiError failures (message + optional code) from the reused api-client methods. A rejected decision (approve/reject returning a non-ok response) is caught and rendered as an inline error without a manual reload; the empty queue is a distinct non-error state.
